lines.trans: If Spartak wins, I am buying beer for everyone!
He has been owing me a bottle of whiskey for half a year.
And I am constantly looking out for your health.
Thank you, of course, Vitya, for such concern.
But if I were in your place I would not worry.
Let's test that right now!
Bet you that I will drink three glasses of beer faster?
What are you and I betting on right now?
If you win, I will give you a case of whiskey.
And if I win, you will hand over the ticket!
Fine, but do not touch the other person's glasses with your hands!
Alright, well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Можете дать мне не двадцать, а десять тысяч.
examples.trans: You can give me ten thousand instead of twenty.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'box, crate' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Выиграешь ты — я дам тебе ящик виски.
examples.trans: If you win, I will give you a case of whiskey.

examples.text: Я настоящий хозяин этого билета, верните мне его!
examples.trans: I am the real owner of that ticket, return it to me!

examples.text: Перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: Someone tipped over the rubbish bins.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.text: Он мне бутылку виски уже полгода отдаёт.
examples.trans: He has been owing me a bottle of whiskey for half a year.

examples.text: А если выиграю я, ты отдашь билет!
examples.trans: And if I win, you will hand over the ticket!

examples.text: Уговор дороже денег, отдавай мне билет.
examples.trans: A deal is a deal, hand the ticket over to me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'ticket' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Видишь, к сожалению, достался только один билет.
examples.trans: You see, unfortunately, I only got one ticket.

examples.text: А если выиграю я, ты отдашь билет!
examples.trans: And if I win, you will hand over the ticket!

examples.text: Уговор дороже денег, отдавай мне билет.
examples.trans: A deal is a deal, hand the ticket over to me.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Хорошо, но чужие бокалы руками не трогать!
examples.trans: Fine, but do not touch the other person's glasses with your hands!

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, сейчас принесу.
examples.trans: Alright, Viktor Petrovich, I will bring it right now.

examples.text: Хорошо, спасибо вам и всего доброго.
examples.trans: Alright, thank you and all the best.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other's').

examples.text: Хорошо, но чужие бокалы руками не трогать!
examples.trans: Fine, but do not touch the other person's glasses with your hands!

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Это чужая сумка.
examples.trans: That's someone else's bag.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hands' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хорошо, но чужие бокалы руками не трогать!
examples.trans: Fine, but do not touch the other person's glasses with your hands!

examples.text: Витя, мои бокалы руками не трогать, помнишь?
examples.trans: Vitya, do not touch my glasses with your hands, remember?

examples.text: Дай руку.
examples.trans: Give me your hand.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to disturb', paired with 'тронуть'.

examples.text: Хорошо, но чужие бокалы руками не трогать!

examples.text: Бокалы не трогать, помнишь?
examples.trans: Do not touch the glasses, remember?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Alright, well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Ладно, забирай, но я это запомню!
examples.trans: Fine, take it, but I will remember this!

examples.text: Такую краску на случай кражи в мешки кладут.
examples.trans: They put such paint in bags in case of theft.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А мне Марина на годовщину тапки подарила.
examples.trans: And Marina gave me slippers for our anniversary.

examples.text: Ладно, ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Alright, well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: Ладно, ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Alright, well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Я готов прямо сейчас бросить вашу Катю.
examples.trans: I am ready to break up with your Katya right now.

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'here we go, let's go', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.text: Ладно, ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Alright, well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Ну что, все готовы? Поехали!
examples.trans: Well then, is everyone ready? Let's go!

examples.text: Мы поедем домой.
examples.trans: We'll go home.
